stages.summary: Play the opening mission Gone Fishing and finish Chapter 1. Before the chapter ends, deal with the game's only missable trophy: one of the 18 meditation spots for Positive Mental Attitude sits at Jason's house, reached in the morning scene with Lucia after the mission Down to Earth, and that house cannot be revisited once Chapter 1 is over. Everything else in this stage is plain story progress.
tips: After Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning and follow her out to the balcony to meditate.
Make a manual save at the start of Chapter 1 and keep it until the meditation is done.
Nothing else in Chapter 1 can be missed — relax and learn the game.
stages.title: Chapter 1 — and the one trophy you can lose

stages.summary: Work through Chapters 2, 3 and 4 and their named missions (Breakfast Run, The Cartel Heist, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown, Operation Savage Glory). Both protagonists are playable from Chapter 2, and the stranger strands open up: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have a final mission in this stretch, and Bret's strand brings the unique-animal hunt. Take strands as they appear instead of stockpiling them. As you travel, scan vehicles and study animals with the binoculars — that progress already counts toward the 100% checklist later.
stages.time: The long middle of the story
tips: Finish each stranger strand when it appears; five of the eight strands Strangers & Freaks needs are here.
Scan vehicles (200 of 277) and study animals (100 of 255) as you go — future checklist progress, free of charge.
Keep a manual save at the start and end of each chapter; there is no mission replay.
stages.title: Chapters 2 to 4 — the story, with strands as they appear

stages.summary: Complete the final mission for the gold story trophy, You Gotta Know When to Get Off. Save manually first. After the credits the game puts you back in free roam and the 100% completion checklist appears under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion — everything from here on is open-world cleanup, and nothing is locked behind the story any more.
tips: Make a manual save immediately before the final mission.
Once the credits end, check the newly revealed 100% checklist before planning the cleanup.
stages.title: The finale — finish the story

stages.summary: Work the checklist the story unlocked, which is what the gold A Long Road trophy measures. It is lenient overall — roughly 60% of true completion — but a handful of categories demand everything: robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests. You need 70 of the 80 challenges, so skip the ones you hate. This stage carries the checklist-heavy trophies: gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, a drone-race win at all 14 locations, 250 stunts on the way to the checklist's 300, 50 challenges, 100 vehicles discovered and all 52 areas of Leonida explored.
tips: Clear the must-complete categories first; use the lenient ones to top the percentage up.
Combine trips: one drive per region moves stunts, vehicles, areas and challenges together.
The checklist's own counts (200 vehicles scanned, 100 animals studied) are the real targets, not the round numbers.
stages.title: The 100% checklist — the long grind

stages.summary: Finish what the checklist did not force: the remaining stranger strands (8 in total for Strangers & Freaks), the robbery set — 5 bank vaults, an armored truck, one illegal operation per gang, a silent jewelry store — and the money trophies: launder $250,000 of marked bills, spend $100,000, buy all 8 garages and register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app. Much of this overlaps the stage 4 grind, so several counters will already be close.
tips: Robberies feed the laundering trophy — keep marked bills moving through your contacts.
The partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) need both protagonists together; do them in one session.
Collectible Cards and WAiNK spots are long-tail: sweep them region by region, not all at the end.
stages.title: Cleanup — strands, robberies and money

stages.summary: Sweep up the hidden one-offs: the unscheduled airport departure, the Rhino tank, the Ocean Beach cocktail, the showroom escape, the bowling alley, the drive-by bowling, and the handful whose exact triggers the published guides had not pinned down when this guide was written (Personal Best, Bad Luck I Guess, The Truth Is Out There among them). For those, the honest method is to check the cited sources for the current confirmed trigger rather than grind on a guess. Actions Speak Louder (500 Criminal Profile actions) normally pops by itself during normal play. When the 54th trophy lands, the platinum follows on its own.
tips: For every unconfirmed trigger, read the cited PowerPyx or EGamers page first — they update as the community confirms things.
Do not invent methods for the vague descriptions; a wrong grind wastes more time than a short read.
The platinum needs no step of its own: it unlocks with the last of the other 54.
stages.title: Odd jobs — and the platinum

summary: One playthrough, roughly 200 hours, difficulty about 4/10 (PowerPyx's estimate). All 55 trophies are offline and single-player — the official list has no online trophies. Two habits carry the whole run: there is no mission replay, so keep a manual save at the start and end of every chapter (the game gives you 15 manual slots plus an autosave), and leave cheats off from beginning to end, because they disable trophies and saving and only unlock after the story anyway. The stages below are built from the official trophy descriptions: chapter order first, then the checklist the finale unlocks, then cleanup.
title: Roadmap to the platinum
